titulo: Adjectival nouns: Das Gute, etwas Neues, alles Gute

aula.objetivo: Turn adjectives and participles into nouns (das Neue, etwas Neues, der Deutsche, ein Bekannter, der Reisende), with a capital letter and the adjective ending.

sessao.titulo: Das Gute, etwas Neues, alles Gute

blocos.titulo: The adjective that becomes a noun, step by step
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: in German, any adjective can become a NOUN, and then it takes a CAPITAL letter: «gut» → «das Gute» (the good). STEP 2: after «DAS», the adjective takes «-e»: «das Gute», «das Neue», «das Wichtigste» (the most important thing), «das Schöne». English often adds "thing": "the important thing" = «das Wichtige». STEP 3: after «ETWAS», «NICHTS», «VIEL», «WENIG», the adjective takes «-ES» — and, just like English, it comes AFTER the word: «etwas Neues» (something new), «nichts Gutes» (nothing good), «viel Interessantes» (a lot of interesting things). STEP 4: after «ALLES», it takes «-E»: «alles Gute» (all the best). STEP 5: use these for abstract ideas: «das Wichtigste» (the most important thing), «das Beste» (the best). STEP 6: common questions and wishes: «Gibt es etwas Neues?» (Anything new?), «Ich wünsche dir alles Gute» (I wish you all the best).
blocos.comparacao: English does this too, partly: "something new", "nothing good", "the rich", "the poor". German does it with every adjective, writes it with a capital letter, and picks the ending according to the word before it.

tabela.exemplo: das Gute, das Neue, das Wichtigste, das Schöne
